finding.claim: The verifier's result cache only records exp/nbf when the payload has a numeric iat. A token with exp but no iat is cached for the full cacheTTL (default 600000 ms) and can still be accepted from the cache after its exp has passed. The same applies to nbf. Preconditions: caching is enabled and the issuer omits iat (for example noTimestamp, or a third-party issuer). The attacker needs a token that was verified while still valid.
finding.source: An attacker-held JWT that has `exp` but no `iat`, submitted to verify() both before and after exp.
finding.sink: The cache hit path in verify() returns the cached payload as valid, skipping the exp validator in verifyToken.

trace.note: hasIat = typeof payload.iat === 'number'. It is false when iat is absent.
The block that sets cacheValue[1] (nbf) and cacheValue[2] (exp) only runs when hasIat is true.
cacheValue[2] is 0, so it falls back to maxTTL = now + clockTolerance + cacheTTL (default 10 minutes).
A cache hit is evaluated against the [value, min, max] range only. max is later than exp, so the entry is still treated as valid.
handleCachedResult returns the cached payload and never re-runs the exp check at lines 304-323.

finding.guards_checked: verifyToken's exp validator runs only on a cache miss. cacheTTL bounds the window but does not tie it to exp. maxAge is applied only inside the hasIat branch. Nothing else compares the cached entry's exp to the current time.
